title: William Carey
hookLine: a poor shoemaker who taught himself languages sails to India: expect great things, attempt great things

lines: A BOOK PROPPED UP AS HE WORKS.
A HOMEMADE MAP ON THE WALL.
cards: A cobbler's bench in an English village. A young shoemaker sits mending boots, and propped up in front of him, the story goes, is a book in Latin or Greek, open while he works.
On the wall hangs a homemade map of the world, with notes about the peoples of each land. He's poor. He has no university degree.
He has taught himself to read languages his neighbors have never seen. And he has a question the older ministers would rather not hear.

teach.b: His question was simple. Jesus told his disciples to go into all the world. Did that still apply to ordinary Christians, or was it only for the apostles?
Carey, by now a Baptist preacher as well as a shoemaker, thought it still applied.
A story is told that when he raised it at a meeting of ministers, an older man told him to sit down: if God wanted to reach the nations, God would do it without him. Carey didn't sit down for long.

teach.h: ENLARGE THE PLACE OF THY TENT.
teach.b: He wrote a pamphlet arguing his case, and then he preached a sermon on a verse from Isaiah: "Enlarge the place of thy tent, and let them stretch forth the curtains of thine habitations: spare not, lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes".
Out of that sermon, people remember a motto in two halves: expect great things from God, attempt great things for God. Notice the order.

Expect comes first: the great things are looked for from God before they're attempted for God. Not long after, a missionary society was formed, and Carey sailed for India with his family. It was hard.
Money ran short, there was illness and grief at home, and fruit came slowly.
With colleagues he set up a press and a college, and spent his life translating the Bible into languages of India, including Bengali. Indian scholars and Christians worked alongside him.
And later readers have asked hard questions about how missions traveled with empire. That's tomorrow's story. Today's is a shoemaker who looked at a map and refused to make his tent smaller.

how: Baptists and other Protestants remember Carey as a pioneer of the modern missionary movement, and churches in India remember the translation work of Carey and his Indian colleagues.

games.q: you're a young shoemaker at a ministers' meeting. you ask whether Christians should still carry the gospel to all the world, and an older man tells you to sit down. what do you do?
o: sit down and drop it for good.
write your case down, preach on it, and sail.
leave the church and go it alone.
games.why: he wrote a pamphlet, preached on enlarge the place of thy tent, and sailed for India with his family.

practice: Picture your own tent, the size of your life right now, and one thing you've stopped hoping for because it seemed too big: a course, a reconciliation, a book, a move, a gift you'd love to give.
Don't plan the whole thing; just let yourself expect it for a minute. If you pray, bring it to God; if you don't, hold it in your mind.
